title: Localhost Port 11434: Local AI in 30 Seconds

structure_breakdown.hook: 0-4s: Terminal prompt friction vs single command
structure_breakdown.setup: 4-10s: One-line install and execution across OS
structure_breakdown.demonstration: 18-28s: Querying localhost:11434 REST API in code

dialogue_and_action.voiceover: Tired of configuring CUDA drivers just to test an open-weight model locally?
dialogue_and_action.visual_action: Close-up of developer terminal showing a failed C++ compilation error, quickly cleared.

dialogue_and_action.voiceover: With Ollama, running open models across macOS, Linux, or Windows takes a single command.
dialogue_and_action.visual_action: Clean terminal typing 'ollama run llama3' with instant model prompt ready.

dialogue_and_action.voiceover: It runs a background service on localhost port 11434, giving you a full REST API for your local scripts with zero per-token costs.
dialogue_and_action.visual_action: Split screen: terminal on left, Python code sending HTTP POST request to localhost:11434 on right, receiving streaming tokens.

dialogue_and_action.voiceover: Just make sure your hardware fits: 7B models need about 4 to 5 gigabytes of VRAM to keep streaming fast and avoid CPU fallback.
dialogue_and_action.visual_action: Clean graphics showing 7B Q4 (~4-5GB VRAM) and 14B (~8-10GB VRAM) memory sizing badges.

dialogue_and_action.voiceover: Get up and running with open models locally today.
dialogue_and_action.visual_action: Ollama documentation page with quickstart commands.
dialogue_and_action.on_screen_text: ollama.com — Available for macOS, Linux, Windows
